clue.text: Have fun returning purchase

indicators.note: returning tells the solver to read the word for purchase backwards

parts.note: purchase is mechanical advantage or grip, as given by a lever

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys themselves taking back something they bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like shopping but means leverage: LEVER, read backwards because of 'returning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to make merry and enjoy oneself greatly.

clue.text: Garment can be about twelve inches

indicators.note: be about means the tin word goes around the measure, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
twelve inches is a foot, written A FT

explanation.surface: A tin can is said to be roughly a foot across, like some garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twelve inches' is A FOOT, abbreviated A FT; 'be about' puts that AFT between C and AN of CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A caftan is a long loose tunic worn in the Middle East, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Make Leo eat it and become weak

indicators.note: Make here means form something new out of the following words, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Forcing a lion called Leo to eat something until he grows feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is the anagram signal: the letters of LEO EAT IT rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To etiolate is to grow pale and sickly, as a plant kept from light loses its vigour.

clue.text: Frenchman requesting cover up job

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
requesting means asking

explanation.surface: A Frenchman asks for a job concealing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Masking is the work of covering surfaces, as decorators do with tape before painting.

clue.text: In concert to win the lady?

parts.note: taken as written
to win something is to get it
the lady is referred to as her

explanation.surface: A suitor hopes a concert will help him woo a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together means acting jointly, in unison with others.

clue.text: Remark that amounts to nothing

parts.note: a statement whose whole content is a refusal to say anything, the stock phrase a politician gives reporters

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment on something insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal refusal to answer, so it says nothing at all.

clue.text: Acted as front-runner the wrong way

definitions.text: Acted as front-runner the wrong way

parts.words: Acted as front-runner the wrong way
parts.note: literally, someone went in front but took the others off course; idiomatically, misled or corrupted

explanation.surface: A race leader takes the wrong route.
explanation.definitionFit: To have misled someone is to have guided them off the right path, morally or physically.

clue.text: Double turn by late Russian dramatist

indicators.note: Double means the word for turn is written twice in a row

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
L is an abbreviation for late, as in the late (deceased)

explanation.surface: A dead Russian playwright did a double turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a nineteenth-century writer of plays such as The Government Inspector, born in the Russian Empire.

clue.text: Endorsement showing one's in Virginia

indicators.note: in means the contraction is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia
one's is I'S, one as the Roman numeral I, plus 's for is

explanation.surface: A document proves someone is currently in Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official stamp in a passport, an endorsement permitting entry.

clue.text: Blow that wasn't landed, possibly

parts.note: a boxing punch thrown with one hand, read as a fish that got off the line and so was never landed

explanation.surface: A punch that missed its target.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, a punch with the weaker fist curving in is a standard blow; read whimsically, a fish that escaped the angler's barb.

clue.text: Cromwell's son-in-law takes one recipe to school

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions
Eton is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A Puritan relative brings a cookery recipe to his school.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is the prescription abbreviation (as in Rx).
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ireton, a Parliamentarian general, married Oliver Cromwell's daughter Bridget.

clue.text: Palindromic female

indicators.note: Palindromic says the answer reads identically from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman whose name reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Close enough to concern one deeply

definitions.text: Close enough to concern one deeply

parts.words: Close enough to concern one deeply
parts.note: literally not far from where one lives; figuratively touching a personal nerve

explanation.surface: Something so near that it worries a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that hits close to one's own house affects one personally.

clue.text: Ostracise a high scorer in snooker

definitions.meaning: to shut someone out by voting against them
the black is the snooker ball worth seven points, the most on the table

explanation.surface: A top snooker player is shunned by colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British cue game; its black ball scores most.
explanation.definitionFit: Club members once voted to exclude someone by dropping a dark ball in the urn; in snooker the dark ball scores seven.

clue.text: Disagreed about being punished

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
punished by whipping, lashed

explanation.surface: People quarrelled over a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions that clashed conflicted, so the people disagreed.

clue.text: Stiff, albeit in a way bent

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
bent into a curve, arched

explanation.surface: Something rigid, though curved in some fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A starched collar has been treated to make it rigid; figuratively a starchy manner is formal.

clue.text: Henry, being 7, is a swimmer

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
7 across means misled; being misled or going astray is erring

explanation.surface: A man called Henry, misled, is a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' points to the 7-across answer, whose sense of going wrong gives ERRING.
explanation.definitionFit: A herring is a fish of the North Atlantic, so it swims.

clue.text: Oriental attribute of fair play

parts.note: E for East, Oriental
an attribute is a characteristic or quality

explanation.surface: An Eastern characteristic of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair play means treating all sides alike, giving them the same standing.

clue.text: Allowance for writers one gets on with

parts.note: pens are writing implements
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money set aside for authors to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a regular payment, an allowance on retirement.

clue.text: Mix up in a motor-cycle trial

definitions.meaning: a cross-country motorbike race over rough ground

explanation.surface: Confusion at an off-road bike race.
explanation.definitionFit: To jumble letters is to muddle them; a motocross event over rough terrain is also called by this word.

clue.text: Break a piece of sculpture

definitions.meaning: a statue of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to bust is to break; a sculpted head and shoulders is also called by this word.

clue.text: State in which one is without a hope

indicators.note: in which one is signals that the state lies concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A condition of hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a condition of mind but is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the United States, in the West, capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: A facial feature starts getting painful

parts.note: the chin is part of the face

indicators.note: starts takes only the opening letter of getting

explanation.surface: A facial feature starts to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sore and throbbing is hurting, so it is painful.

clue.text: Craft to run on time

parts.note: to run away is to flee

explanation.surface: A boat must leave on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of ships or vessels is a navy's group of craft.

clue.text: Simply a computer

parts.note: a basic calculating device, frame with beads on wires

explanation.surface: Just a calculating machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is an ancient counting frame, the simplest calculator.

clue.text: Practised, no doubt, by the daily woman at home

definitions.text: Practised, no doubt, by the daily woman at home

parts.words: Practised, no doubt, by the daily woman at home
parts.note: a cleaner, called a daily help in Britain, doing her own housework would assist herself

explanation.surface: A charwoman's domestic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or 'help' is British for a cleaning woman who comes in by day.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving oneself without outside assistance; the cleaner helping in her own house does just that.

clue.text: A lawful right that's incompatible

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement that conflicts with something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas foreign to one's nature are at odds with it, as in 'alien to his principles'.

clue.text: Foreshadowed the last of the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified Portuguese wine
the last of something means it has ended

explanation.surface: Finishing the last bottle hinted at what was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that portended a future event served as an omen or warning of it.
